marks.gloss_en: a mouse entered with a loaf and crumbs were found: bedika is still required, for a mouse does not crumble
R' Yehuda: bedika at three times -- the night of the 14th, the morning of the 14th, and the hour of biur
Chachamim: whenever he has not yet checked he checks -- even within the festival, even after it
R' Yehuda's three bedikot are three separate obligations, corresponding to the three הַשְׁבָּתוֹת in the Torah
R' Yehuda (per Rav Yosef): one who did not check at these three times checks no more
R' Yehuda (per Mar Zutra's version): one who did not check at ONE of these three times checks no more
R' Yehuda too means: if he did not check at one time, he checks at the next -- the three times are fallbacks
R' Yehuda: bedika only before the issur takes hold, not after it
